meaning:
θερμαίνω
(θερμός), [in LXX chiefly for חָמַם ;]
to warm, heat; mid., to warm oneself: Mrk.14:54, 67, Jhn.18:18, 25 Jas.2:16.†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: Peter had followed him from a distance, until he came into the court of the high priest. He was sitting with the officers, and warming himself in the light of…
Now the servants and the officers were standing there, having made a fire of coals, for it was cold. They were warming themselves. Peter was with them…
and one of you tells them, “Go in peace. Be warmed and filled;” yet you didn’t give them the things the body needs, what good is it?
